PullRequest.Title: sessions: Align unread status icon sizes
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
- keep compact workspace-less chat rows on the shared 16px session status icon sizing
- add unit coverage for unread icon sizing in compact and regular quick-chat presentations
- add blocking component screenshot fixtures for normal and compact Sessions list layouts

## Why
Unread indicators represented the same state but appeared smaller for workspace-less chats because their compact row styling overrode the shared status icon size.

## Validation
- `npm run compile`
- `npm run hygiene`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --grep "renders compact and regular quick-chat rows consistently"`
- dark and light component screenshots for normal and compact layouts

Scenarios.Scenario: Render unread workspace-less quick-chat and workspace-backed session rows in the Sessions list, in normal and compact view modes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The list renderer creates/reuses a status-icon DOM node, applies the quick-chat class, and the browser performs style calculation/layout/paint before the row is visible. The diff only removes quick-chat-specific 12px/14px size overrides, so icons inherit the existing 16px base dimensions; it adds no JavaScript work to this critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with the number of currently rendered/virtualized rows, not the total session history. The CSS change removes declarations from one existing selector and does not increase effective row cardinality or update frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering and style/layout work execute serially on the UI thread; status-icon updates are cached by glyph/variant and the virtualized list reuses row templates. The diff does not add scheduling, parallelism, or bursts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SessionStatusIcon retains its existing current-glyph cache, while list virtualization limits live row DOM. Cold and warm behavior are unchanged because the CSS cascade does not alter cache keys, reuse, coalescing, or invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the complete production diff is deletion-only CSS, and the renderer/status-widget trace shows no new calls, allocations, listeners, animations, or external boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact paint cost varies by platform and number of visible rows, but a static 12-to-16px inherited icon-size change within the existing 16px slot does not establish additional repeated layout or paint work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The production change alters static icon dimensions and removes CSS override work; it does not introduce or amplify a concrete performance mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the SessionsFlatList quick-chat unit test for compact and regular presentations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each of the two bounded renderQuickChat invocations lays out one row and now performs one synchronous getComputedStyle read to assert the icon font size. This is test-only and not reachable from the product Sessions view.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly two one-session render invocations in one unit test; no data-dependent collection or event-frequency growth.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two render calls and style reads execute synchronously and serially in the browser test runner.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each harness is isolated; no production cache behavior is changed. Browser style caches may satisfy the read, but the test remains bounded even on a cold style calculation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the changed test directly shows one getComputedStyle call per helper invocation and the assertion invokes the helper twice.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser style-resolution duration varies, but cardinality is fixed at two and has no user-facing runtime impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Although getComputedStyle can force synchronous style resolution, the work is bounded to two test-only calls and is not a realistic product performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Generate normal and compact component screenshots for unread status icons
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The fixture runner renders two in-memory sessions, performs a local SessionsList.reveal that linearly scans the two-session fixture and updates the tree focus/selection, then captures and compares the screenshot. The screenshot work is on the blocking CI fixture path, not the product runtime path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Component screenshot capture and baseline comparison initiated by screenshot fixtures
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two newly registered fixtures, multiplied only by the themed fixture runner's configured theme count; each fixture renders two sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These two unread-status-icon screenshot captures did not exist before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The fixtures are marked blocksCi, so their bounded capture/comparison must complete for the relevant CI check, but they are off all end-user product paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two new fixtures, each with exactly two sessions; effective cardinality is fixed. Themed execution may multiply these bounded fixtures by the fixture group's configured themes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within each fixture, list rendering/reveal is serial UI-thread work. Fixture-runner concurrency is external to this diff; no limiter or burst behavior is changed by the fixture implementation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fixtures construct isolated list instances and synthetic session data, so there is no warm production cache. The diff adds no persistent cache, retained key, or invalidation behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that two screenshot fixtures are added and that reveal is a local O(n) tree operation over n=2; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network call is introduced in the fixture code itself.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The runner's per-screenshot duration and theme count are not established in the changed code, but the added fixture count and per-fixture data size are tightly bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The intentional, fixed-size CI coverage adds bounded test time only and does not create a user-visible performance regression or an unbounded CI mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and every diff hunk. Traced production row rendering, status-icon caching, compact CSS layout, the unit-test style read, fixture reveal behavior, and screenshot-boundary cardinality. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression was found.
